responseBinding.questionText: Document requiring certification: birth ______

bindings.audiblePhrase: It is my birth certificate. I also have a university transcript, although the organisation has asked for an ordinary scan of that, so it does not need certification.

responseBinding.questionText: Number of certified copies: ______

bindings.audiblePhrase: I first selected two, then checked the application letter again. It asks for three copies, so please put three on the appointment form.

responseBinding.questionText: Appointment day: ______

bindings.audiblePhrase: Wednesday at ten forty would be best. Friday was my first thought, but I need to post the application before then.

responseBinding.questionText: Appointment time: ______

bindings.audiblePhrase: Wednesday at ten forty would be best. Friday was my first thought, but I need to post the application before then.

responseBinding.questionText: Photo identification to bring: ______

bindings.audiblePhrase: Then I will bring my passport, along with the original certificate. I will leave the old driving licence at home so there is no confusion.

responseBinding.questionText: Chosen return method: ______

bindings.audiblePhrase: Please use the courier. I considered collecting them, but I will be outside Wellington for work the next day and tracking would be reassuring.

responseBinding.questionText: Which professional will certify Tessa’s copies?

bindings.audiblePhrase: That is noted. A solicitor is available at that appointment. A Justice of the Peace also certifies copies in many situations, but none is rostered here on Wednesday morning.

responseBinding.questionText: What must be written clearly beside the certifier’s signature?

bindings.audiblePhrase: The certifier compares each copy with the original and adds the required statement. Beside the signature, the date must be written clearly. Please do not write on the copies yourself before the appointment.

responseBinding.questionText: What should Tessa bring to show the receiving organisation’s requirements?

bindings.audiblePhrase: Yes, bring the application letter. It lets the solicitor check whether the receiving organisation has specified particular wording. A screenshot on your phone is not necessary if you have the letter.

responseBinding.questionText: What will appear on both the confirmation email and courier label?

bindings.audiblePhrase: Your confirmation email will contain a reference number. The same reference number appears on the courier label and in the tracking message. It is more reliable than searching by your surname.

responseBinding.questionText: Which instruction does Maeve give about the buoyancy aid?
responseBinding.correctOptionText: wait until your surname is called before taking it

bindings.audiblePhrase: Buoyancy aids are arranged by size near the door, but please do not pick one up immediately. I have the booking list and will call surnames in order. Wait until you hear yours before taking an aid; we need to record the size issued.

responseBinding.questionText: Which instruction does Maeve give about the whistle?
responseBinding.correctOptionText: hand it back separately from the rest of the equipment

bindings.audiblePhrase: Whistles arrive clipped to the aids, although they are logged separately. At the end, do not put yours into the general equipment crate. Unclip it and hand it back separately; reception staff count them before the next group.

responseBinding.questionText: Which instruction does Maeve give about the spare paddle?
responseBinding.correctOptionText: show it to the assistant at the riverside gate

bindings.audiblePhrase: Each pair has a spare paddle. Before you carry it down the path, show it to the assistant at the riverside gate. She will check the blade number against your boat; the check is not done at the equipment rack.

responseBinding.questionText: Which instruction does Maeve give about the dry bag?
responseBinding.correctOptionText: collect it from reception after the safety talk

bindings.audiblePhrase: We also lend dry bags for small essentials. They remain behind the desk while I give this safety talk, so do not take one from the bench. When the talk ends, collect the bag from reception and write its number on your locker slip.

responseBinding.questionText: Which instruction does Maeve give about the throw line?
responseBinding.correctOptionText: leave it where it is until a staff member removes it

bindings.audiblePhrase: The throw line is already secured beside the bank assistant's position. Leave it where it is when you move the boats; a trained staff member will remove it if needed. Beginners should not carry it to the water or practise with it today.

responseBinding.questionText: Which changing room should beginners use today?

bindings.audiblePhrase: Now, changing rooms. The upstairs room looks larger, but building work has closed it this week. Use the ground-floor changing room beside reception. The outdoor shelter is for wet equipment after the session, not for changing clothes.

responseBinding.questionText: Who enters the water first?

bindings.audiblePhrase: Once changed, place bags in the lockers and meet beside the equipment rack. We launch in a fixed order. The instructor enters first and waits downstream. Paddlers then launch one at a time. The bank assistant goes last after checking that nothing has been left behind.

responseBinding.questionText: What do two short whistle blasts mean?

bindings.audiblePhrase: You may hear three possible signals. One short whistle means look towards the instructor and wait for a hand signal. Two short blasts mean gather near the bank. A continuous blast means leave the water at the nearest safe landing point. Today we will practise the two-blast signal before travelling upstream.

responseBinding.questionText: Who makes the decision to cancel a session?

bindings.audiblePhrase: People often ask whether light rain cancels a session. Usually it does not. We check river level, wind and official weather information together. If conditions become unsafe, the centre manager—not an individual participant—makes the cancellation decision and sends a text to the booking contact.

responseBinding.questionText: What should paddlers do with damaged equipment after returning?

bindings.audiblePhrase: When we return, carry the boats to the marked stands. Leave wet buoyancy aids on the ventilated rail, not in your locker. Rinse the paddles at the hose, but report any damage before you clean it, so staff can see the problem clearly.

responseBinding.questionText: What revision do the producers agree for the opening headlines?
responseBinding.correctOptionText: shorten it to one sentence per story

bindings.audiblePhrase: So for the opening headlines, we shorten the summary and keep only one sentence per story. I had considered dropping the local arts item entirely, but its full report appears later and still needs a headline.

responseBinding.questionText: What revision do the producers agree for the recorded market interview?
responseBinding.correctOptionText: edit it to a maximum of two minutes

bindings.audiblePhrase: Next is the recorded market interview. The raw interview lasts four minutes forty. The strongest answer begins after a long introduction, so trim the insert to two minutes and start with the vendor explaining the price change.

responseBinding.questionText: What revision do the producers agree for the traffic bulletin?
responseBinding.correctOptionText: move it to an earlier position

bindings.audiblePhrase: The traffic bulletin is scheduled after the culture review, yet the road closure begins during our broadcast. Move that bulletin earlier, immediately after the opening headlines, so the information reaches commuters in time.

responseBinding.questionText: What revision do the producers agree for the empty studio-guest slot?

bindings.audiblePhrase: Use selected listener messages instead. We already have permission to broadcast five, and the presenter can read three contrasting responses. That replaces the cancelled guest without pretending we have a new interview.

responseBinding.questionText: What revision do the producers agree for the closing trail?
responseBinding.correctOptionText: refer to a topic instead of a named person

bindings.audiblePhrase: For the closing trail, the recorded version advertises next week’s guest by name. Since the booking is not confirmed, we should replace the name with the programme topic rather than delete the whole trail.

responseBinding.questionText: All changes will be entered in the shared ______.

bindings.audiblePhrase: Better to put every change in the shared rundown. A photograph cannot show whether the presenter, studio manager and news desk are looking at the same version.

responseBinding.questionText: The producers will backtime from the fixed ______.

bindings.audiblePhrase: Right. We should backtime from the fixed news bulletin at half past the hour. Its start cannot move, so our programme must finish cleanly before that feed opens.

responseBinding.questionText: The final market insert will last ______.

bindings.audiblePhrase: Exactly. With the market insert limited to two minutes, the revised total becomes twenty-seven minutes forty. That leaves twenty seconds for the continuity cue and a safe handover.

responseBinding.questionText: The continuity cue will be shown in ______.

bindings.audiblePhrase: This time put the continuity cue in red. Do not colour the whole final line; only the words that tell the presenter to stop and hand to news.

responseBinding.questionText: Before rehearsal, the producers will check the ______.

bindings.audiblePhrase: And the continuity cue is red, with pronunciations checked before rehearsal. That should make the programme both accurate and calm under live conditions.

responseBinding.questionText: Urban combustion releases ______.

bindings.audiblePhrase: The first precursor is nitrogen oxides, often written as NOx. In cities, important sources include vehicles and combustion. These gases undergo oxidation in the atmosphere. The chemistry differs between day and night, but both pathways can ultimately produce nitric acid.

responseBinding.questionText: Agriculture is an important regional source of ______.

bindings.audiblePhrase: The second important gas is ammonia. Agricultural activity is a major source over broad regions, although urban sources also exist. Air masses do not respect municipal boundaries, so ammonia formed outside a city can influence particulate nitrate measured within it.

responseBinding.questionText: Oxidation of the first precursor can produce ______.

bindings.audiblePhrase: Now consider the simplified sequence. Nitrogen oxides are oxidised to nitric acid. Nitric acid then reacts with ammonia. One important product is ammonium nitrate, which can enter the fine-particle fraction. This diagram is a teaching simplification: real air contains competing compounds and surfaces.

responseBinding.questionText: Reaction with the second gas can form ______.

bindings.audiblePhrase: Now consider the simplified sequence. Nitrogen oxides are oxidised to nitric acid. Nitric acid then reacts with ammonia. One important product is ammonium nitrate, which can enter the fine-particle fraction. This diagram is a teaching simplification: real air contains competing compounds and surfaces.

responseBinding.questionText: The particle phase is generally favoured by ______.

bindings.audiblePhrase: Whether ammonium nitrate remains in particles depends strongly on temperature. Low temperatures generally favour the particle phase, while warmer conditions encourage some material to return to gases. Relative humidity and the presence of other ions also matter, so temperature alone does not predict every observation. Later, laboratories analyse filter samples for those ions.

responseBinding.questionText: Laboratories analyse ______ for nitrate and ammonium ions.

bindings.audiblePhrase: Whether ammonium nitrate remains in particles depends strongly on temperature. Low temperatures generally favour the particle phase, while warmer conditions encourage some material to return to gases. Relative humidity and the presence of other ions also matter, so temperature alone does not predict every observation. Later, laboratories analyse filter samples for those ions.

responseBinding.questionText: What primarily explains the seasonal shift of nitrate between gas and particle phases?

bindings.audiblePhrase: This helps explain why nitrate often shows a seasonal pattern. A cold winter atmosphere can support particulate nitrate, and a winter inversion may trap pollutants close to the ground. In summer, stronger mixing can dilute local concentrations and greater heat can shift volatile material away from particles.

responseBinding.questionText: What is the main limitation of a total particle-mass measurement?
responseBinding.correctOptionText: It does not distinguish the chemical components of the particles.

bindings.audiblePhrase: Total particle mass remains valuable, but it cannot by itself identify which chemical components produced a peak. Two days may have similar fine-particle mass while one contains more nitrate and the other more organic material or sulfate. Composition measurements therefore change the scientific interpretation.

responseBinding.questionText: Why may a filter measurement underestimate nitrate?
responseBinding.correctOptionText: Some collected ammonium nitrate can evaporate before analysis.

bindings.audiblePhrase: Filters also introduce uncertainty. Ammonium nitrate is semi-volatile. Material collected on a filter can partly evaporate during sampling, transport or storage, especially if temperature changes. A low laboratory result may therefore reflect loss from the filter rather than low nitrate in the original air.

responseBinding.questionText: Which approach best represents the lecturer’s central recommendation?
responseBinding.correctOptionText: Combine multiple measurement methods with precursor and meteorological evidence.

bindings.audiblePhrase: The central lesson is methodological. Nitrate is produced through linked chemical steps, distributed by moving air and observed through imperfect instruments. The best explanation joins the precursor record, the meteorology and more than one measurement method rather than relying on total particle mass alone. It should also report uncertainty openly, distinguish correlation from mechanism, and test whether the same interpretation survives at different sites and times. That caution matters whenever a chemically dynamic pollutant is represented by a single daily number.
